title: Variant
description: A purchasable variant of a product with specific option selections.

id.description: Global ID (GID) uniquely identifying this variant. Used as item.id in checkout.

sku.description: Business-assigned identifier for inventory and fulfillment.

type.description: Barcode standard. Well-known values: UPC, EAN, ISBN, GTIN, JAN.

barcodes.description: Industry-standard product identifiers for cross-reference and correlation.

description.description: Variant description in one or more formats.

categories.description: Variant categories with optional taxonomy identifiers.

price.description: Current selling price. REQUIRED when `pricing` is absent or `pricing.mode` is `public` [PROPOSED: conditional requiredness — see `pricing`]. MUST NOT be present when `pricing.mode` is `quote_required` or `contract_only` [PROPOSED]. MAY be absent or present when `pricing.mode` is `buyer_specific`, or any unrecognized/unknown mode [PROPOSED — see `pricing` for the per-mode rules]. Price is the amount per one whole `quantity_unit.unit` (for example, per lb or per hour); when `quantity_unit` is absent, it is per `each`. Line total is `price × quantity × 10^-scale`, computed and rounded once by the Business; `totals` remain authoritative.

pricing.description: [PROPOSED — requires a TC-approved Enhancement Proposal] Pricing state of this variant in this response. `mode` describes how price is (or is not) advertised to the caller of *this response* — it is a property of the response, not a fixed property of the variant: the same variant may be `buyer_specific` to an anonymous caller and carry a numeric price for a linked buyer. `mode` is an OPEN vocabulary (not a closed enum): well-known values are `public` (default; a numeric price is advertised and `price` is REQUIRED), `buyer_specific` (price depends on the caller; a numeric `price` MAY be present when this response is addressed to a recognized buyer — when present, `mode` MUST remain `buyer_specific` so a Platform can tell the value is specific to that caller; a Platform MUST NOT expose or reuse a buyer-specific price, or any value derived from it such as a product `price_range`, for a different caller; `buyer_specific` does not necessarily mean the amount was mathematically computed just for that one person — the same negotiated/list price may be visible to multiple entitled buyers while remaining non-public; the mode primarily communicates disclosure context, not individualized computation), `quote_required` (no price is advertised; the buyer must request a quote — `price` MUST NOT be present), `contract_only` (no price is advertised; pricing exists only under contract — `price` MUST NOT be present. This describes the unresolved response to a caller who has not established the necessary entitlement; once the Business resolves pricing for a recognized/entitled buyer, the response transitions to `buyer_specific` + `price` — `contract_only` itself remains a genuinely unpriced state). A Platform MUST tolerate `mode` values it does not recognize: an unrecognized `mode` MUST NOT make the payload invalid merely for being unrecognized, and `price` MAY be absent or present alongside it. When a Platform does not recognize a `mode`, it MUST treat the item conservatively as having no usable display price — it MUST NOT interpret a missing price as zero, MUST NOT display an accompanying numeric price as authoritative, and MUST exclude the item from numeric price filtering, sorting, or ranking unless it understands that mode. A generated SDK's binding for `mode` MUST preserve unknown string values rather than failing deserialization on an unrecognized enum member.

mode.description: Pricing mode for this variant in this response. Open vocabulary: well-known values are listed in `examples`, but this is not a closed set — a Business MAY introduce new values, and a Platform MUST tolerate values it does not recognize (see parent `pricing` description for the required safe-fallback behavior).

reason.description: Business-defined machine-readable reason for a non-public mode (for example `contract_or_volume_dependent`). Informational only; consumers MUST NOT infer semantics beyond `mode`.

next_step.description: Well-known values: `request_quote`, meaning a quote-related interaction is available. Identifies a well-known pricing-related interaction the Business wishes to expose in connection with the variant. Its presence does not imply that the interaction is mandatory and does not determine whether a usable price is present: `request_quote` means a quote path is available; `pricing.mode` determines whether obtaining a quote is necessary to obtain a usable price. It MAY coexist with a numeric `price` — for example `buyer_specific` + `price` + `request_quote` (caller already has a usable price; a quote path is additionally available) or `public` + `price` + `request_quote` (a public price exists; the Business also accepts quote requests). `next_step` MUST NOT participate in, or be used to infer, `price` requiredness or range/filter eligibility — those depend solely on `pricing.mode`. Informational only; it defines no quote, RFQ, or identity-linking workflow.

quantity_unit.description: Sale basis this variant's `quantity` is denominated in. The default sale basis is `each`, whose machine identity is (`C62`, 0); `C62` is the UN/CEFACT Rec20 code for one/each. An absent catalog descriptor encodes that default. An `increment` advertises the ordering granularity in steps (for example, `scale` 2 with `increment` 25 sells in 0.25-unit multiples).

list_price.description: List price before discounts (for strikethrough display).

unit_price.description: Price per standard unit of measurement, for shelf-style comparison display. MAY be omitted when unit pricing does not apply.

options.description: Option values that define this variant (e.g., Color: Blue, Size: Large).

media.description: Variant media (images, videos, 3D models). First item is the featured media for listings.

tags.description: Variant tags for categorization and search.

metadata.description: Business-defined custom data extending the standard variant model.

seller.description: Optional seller context for this variant.

allOf.description: [PROPOSED] Neither `price` nor `unit_price` (a per-unit selling price) may be present when the variant advertises `quote_required` or `contract_only` — both known modes are genuinely unpriced states: `quote_required` says a quote is needed to resolve pricing, and `contract_only` describes the unresolved response to a caller who has not established the necessary entitlement. Once the Business resolves pricing for a recognized/entitled buyer, the response transitions to `buyer_specific` + `price` rather than retaining `contract_only` with a price. An unrecognized/unknown `mode` is not constrained by this rule (it checks only these two known literal values, not a closed set on `mode` itself).
[PROPOSED] Price is REQUIRED for publicly priced variants (the default when `pricing` is absent).
[PROPOSED] `unit_price` is derived from the selling price and requires `price` to be present.
